<problem>
For a nonempty finite poset $S$, a linear extension is a total order on its underlying set that extends its partial order. Its order dimension $\dim S$ is the least positive integer $t$ for which there are linear extensions $L_1,\ldots,L_t$ such that $x\le_S y$ if and only if $x\le_{L_i}y$ for every $i$.

For each positive integer $k$, write $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$. Let $\lambda(k)$ be the number of inclusion-maximal intersecting families of subsets of $[k]$: a family $\mathcal F$ is intersecting when $A\cap B\ne\varnothing$ for all $A,B\in\mathcal F$, including $A=B$, and it is inclusion-maximal when no proper larger family of subsets of $[k]$ is intersecting.

Fix an integer $d\ge8$ and put $M_d=\lambda(d-1)+1$. Let $Q_d$ be the poset consisting of all one-element and two-element subsets of $[M_d]$, ordered by inclusion. For a nonempty finite poset $P$, order $P\times Q_d$ by $(p,A)\le(p',A')$ exactly when $p\le_P p'$ and $A\subseteq A'$.

Let $F(d)$ be the supremum of $\dim(P\times Q_d)-\dim P$ as $P$ ranges over all nonempty finite posets with $\dim P\ge3$. Determine $F(d)$ exactly for every integer $d\ge8$.
</problem>

A complete answer to this problem: A complete answer must give an exact value of F(d) for every integer d≥8, as a formula in d or an exhaustive casewise rule, and establish that it equals the stated supremum.

Their run ended: all agents idle, the judge found the proof complete. Read from their record, the answer they ended with is F(d)=d-3 for every integer d≥8.. Their whole record is in your folder, read-only:

- record/finals.md: each agent's last reply, often its write-up.
- record/transcripts/<agent>.md: each agent's whole run: its reasoning summaries, its messages, every file it wrote and ran, and what each run printed.
- workspace/: the folder the team shared, as they left it (code, data, certificates, write-ups).
- agents/<agent>/: each agent's own folder (its scratchpad.py and files).

Your tools: list_files, read_file, grep, write_file (files of your own folder; not inside record/, workspace/ or agents/), and run_python, which runs a Python file of your folder in a sandbox with the team's libraries (NumPy, SciPy, SymPy, mpmath, NetworkX, Sage via passagemath, ...), no network, up to 1200 s a run. 14	## 1. Permutations and a product-dimension lemma
15	
16	For permutations \(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_s\) of a finite set \(V\), put
17	\[
18	T(b,a)=\{i:a\text{ occurs after }b\text{ in }\pi_i\}\qquad(a\ne b).
19	\]
20	
21	We will construct systems with these two properties:
22	
23	1. For each \(a\), the sets \(T(b,a)\), \(b\ne a\), are pairwise intersecting.
24	2. For each \(a\), there is a coloring
25	   \[
26	   c_a:[s]\longrightarrow[3]
27	   \]
28	   such that every \(T(b,a)\) contains all three colors.
29	
30	The first property says precisely that for any three distinct elements and any distinguished one, some permutation puts the distinguished element last. The colorings in the second property may depend on \(a\).
31	
32	Write \(Q(V)\) for the inclusion poset of the singletons and doubletons of \(V\).
33	
34	**Product lemma.** If such a system of \(s\) permutations exists on \(V\), then, for every finite \(P\) with \(t=\dim P\ge3\),
35	\[
36	\dim(P\times Q(V))\le t+s-3. \tag{1}
37	\]
38	
39	**Proof.** A realizer of \(P\) gives an order embedding
40	\[
41	f=(f_1,\ldots,f_t):P\longrightarrow[m]^t
42	\]
43	for some \(m\). Let \(r_i(a)\) be the rank of \(a\) in \(\pi_i\). Keep the coordinates \(f_4,\ldots,f_t\), and introduce
44	\[
45	H_i(p,A)=\max_{a\in A}\bigl(mr_i(a)+f_{c_a(i)}(p)\bigr),
46	\qquad i\in[s]. \tag{2}
47	\]
48	These \(t+s-3\) coordinates are order-preserving.
49	
50	They also reflect order. If \(A\nsubseteq B\), choose \(a\in A\setminus B\). Some permutation puts \(a\) after every member of \(B\), so its \(H_i\)-coordinate separates \((p,A)\) from \((q,B)\), independently of \(p,q\).
51	
52	Now suppose \(A\subseteq B\), but \(p\nleq q\). Choose \(j\) with \(f_j(p)>f_j(q)\). If \(j>3\), a retained coordinate separates them. If \(j\le3\), choose an endpoint \(a\in A\) and an index \(i\) of color \(j\) at \(a\) which puts \(a\) after the other endpoint of \(B\), when there is one. Property 2 supplies such an index. Then the maxima in (2) are attained at \(a\), and again the coordinate separates the two elements.
53	
54	Thus (2), together with the retained coordinates, is an order embedding into a product of \(t+s-3\) chains, proving (1). ∎

56	We will prove:

58	> **Construction theorem.** For every \(d\ge8\), there is a system satisfying properties 1 and 2 with \(s=d\) on at least \(\lambda(d-1)+1\) elements. \(\tag{3}\)

98	## 3. A lexicographic construction

100	Let \(\mathcal D\subseteq2^{[s]}\) be closed under complementation. Consider a collection of families \(\mathcal A\) such that every \(\mathcal F\in\mathcal A\):
101	
102	- chooses exactly one member of each complementary pair in \(\mathcal D\);
103	- is intersecting.
104	
105	Order the complementary pairs once and for all. For each \(i\in[s]\), lexicographically order the families, preferring at the first difference the family whose chosen side contains \(i\).
106	
107	If \(\mathcal F,\mathcal G\) first differ at the pair \(\{A,A^c\}\), with \(A\in\mathcal F\), then
108	\[
109	T(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)=A. \tag{7}

136	\]

211	## 5. A bound for the number of upsets
212	
213	Let \(D(n)\) denote the number of upsets of \(B_n\), and write
214	\[
215	W_n=\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}.
216	\]

218	\[
219	D(n)\le3^{W_n}. \tag{15}
220	\]

222	Here is a proof, included to make the argument self-contained.
223	
224	There is an ordered symmetric-chain decomposition of \(B_n\) with the following property:
225	
226	> Between the endpoints of every consecutive three-element segment of a chain, there is another intermediate element belonging to an earlier chain.
227	
228	Construct it recursively. For each old chain
229	\[
230	C=(x_0,\ldots,x_{\ell-1}),
231	\]
232	output, in this order,
233	\[
234	(x_0+n,\ldots,x_{\ell-2}+n)
235	\]

237	\[
238	(x_0,\ldots,x_{\ell-1},x_{\ell-1}+n).
239	\]
240	Process old chains in their previous order. Old three-element segments inherit their earlier intermediate element; the new terminal segment of the long chain uses \(x_{\ell-2}+n\) from the short chain.
241	
242	Reveal an upset's indicator chain by chain. Once earlier chains are known, the unknown values on the current chain form an interval. That interval cannot contain three consecutive elements: the earlier intermediate element would force one endpoint's value. Thus there are at most two unknown values, with at most three monotone assignments.
